name: Tiroler Bauernmarkt & Verkostung
beschreibung:
### Overview
The Innsbruck Market Hall (Markthalle) on the Herzog-Siegmund-Ufer on the banks of the Inn is the culinary showcase of the Tyrol. From Monday to Saturday, farmers, dairies and small family businesses from the valleys of North and East Tyrol bring their handcrafted specialities straight into the provincial capital. At the farmers' market, the air is filled with the aroma of freshly baked farmhouse bread, smoked bacon, spicy alpine cheese and herbal products – against the backdrop of the Nordkette.

### Route & Requirements
A guided market tour with tastings leads through the halls and outdoor stalls of the Market Hall. Led by a food guide, participants learn the stories and production methods behind the regional products. Selected stalls offer tastings, for example of Tyrolean Graukäse, matured mountain cheese, savoury sausages, cloudy apple juice or stone pine schnapps. The route is completely level and largely weather-independent; it is easily accessible for prams and wheelchair users. No particular physical stamina is required. Well-behaved dogs are allowed on a lead at the outdoor stalls, but not inside the hall for hygiene reasons.

### Getting There
The Market Hall is centrally located in Innsbruck's old town right on the Inn promenade. From Innsbruck Central Station it is about a ten-minute walk through Maria-Theresien-Straße, or easily reached by IVB tram and bus lines. Drivers will find paid parking in the car parks around the city centre; arriving by public transport is recommended.

### Tips
Come with a light appetite, as the tasting portions are generous. A reusable cool bag or backpack helps you take home delicacies such as alpine butter, farm honey and bacon fresh. After the tour, a short detour across the Inn bridge to the Mariahilf district with its colourful facades is well worth it.
